feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications/platform leader with clear domain focus and solid progression at NACo. It reads polished and substantive, but it is slightly repetitive, overly dense in places, and could sharpen impact by reducing overlap across skills/projects sections.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative: strong career progression within one organization, culminating in director-level ownership of web, analytics, governance, and multimedia.  
- Good use of scale and scope: metrics like “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and “50+ internal publishers” add credibility and impact.  
- Writing is generally professional and consistent, with strong positioning around public-sector digital transformation and AI-enabled search.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: Core Competencies, Topline Skills, Technical + IT, and Recent Projects overlap significantly. Consolidating these would improve structure and scannability.  
- Add more outcome-focused results beyond activity descriptions, especially in consulting and earlier roles; quantify improvements in engagement, efficiency, adoption, or cost savings where possible.  
- Minor style/grammar consistency issues: “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; “Ranked among the top public universities…” is weak/irrelevant filler; title casing is inconsistent (“Topline Skills,” “Technical + IT”); “French (A2/Learning)” is stylistically awkward—use “French (A2, improving)” or similar.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear seniority and domain focus. It reads well, but it’s slightly dense and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and experience sections.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten the first sentence and foreground scale/sector impact: “Senior digital leader with 12+ years shaping platforms, governance, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications.”
- Replace “Leads” with a parallel, more specific construction: “Expertise spans enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial governance, multimedia production, and AI-enabled search/content experiences.”
- Consider adding one concrete scale marker from recent roles if space allows, e.g., “10,000+ page Drupal migration” or “3.5M annual page views.”
- Standardize style: use either “AI-enabled search and content experiences” or “AI-enabled user experiences,” not both across the CV.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Platforms, governance models and content operations” overlaps heavily with Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “Enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production” is echoed almost verbatim in recent NACo roles.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes that align well with the headline, but this block currently overlaps heavily with the summary and Topline Skills. It would be stronger if tightened to emphasize distinctive leadership-level capabilities rather than repeating adjacent sections.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use more concise, parallel phrasing and remove filler words like “operations” where possible.
- Prioritize the most senior, differentiating strengths: web modernization, governance, analytics, AI search, automation, and public-sector communications.
- Consider this rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial systems • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector and advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream delivery
- Standardize style by replacing “website” with “web” for consistency with the rest of the CV.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multi-channel communications operations” duplicates the header and Topline Skills; consider dropping it.
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” overlaps with the dedicated multimedia skills section; keep only if you want this block to stay broad rather than highly differentiated.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and repeats themes already covered in Work Experience. Tightening phrasing and making outcomes or scope more concrete will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Use consistent action verbs and style: “Led,” “Built,” “Developed,” “Produced”; avoid mixing “designed/built/developed” without a pattern.
- Increase specificity where possible: note audience, scale, platform, or business purpose (for example, legislative content discovery, campaign growth, conference activation).
- Fix style consistency: spell out “10 x 20-foot” instead of “10×20-foot,” and consider “AI-powered” or “AI-enabled” consistently across the CV.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series closely overlap with recent NACo roles; keep this section project-focused and avoid restating responsibilities.
- “Editorial storytelling,” “web features,” and “distribution across website, email and social channels” echo broader skills sections; prioritize unique project outcomes or deliverables.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the NACo role below and Recent Projects. Tighten it around consulting impact, transformation outcomes, and what is new since returning as a consultant.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper positioning line: “Advising NACo on enterprise digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations, and web modernization as an external consultant.”
- Replace generic verbs (“consult,” “advise,” “deliver”) with outcome-oriented phrasing: “Redesigned workflows,” “launched campaign microsites,” “improved governance,” “led AI search initiative.”
- Consolidate into 3–4 bullets and add metrics where possible: number of sites/pages supported, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, publishing time reduced, search success/engagement gains.
- Example rewrite: “Lead enterprise web and communications improvements for NACo, redesigning digital workflows, analytics, and governance to support coordinated cross-channel publishing.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “AI-enabled search initiative” duplicates the Recent Projects entry; keep this bullet high-level here and leave technical detail to Projects.
- Drupal/CMS/front-end execution overlaps with the prior Director role; emphasize consultant-level transformation and new initiatives instead.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground the biggest outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management points covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope/result line: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web modernization, analytics, governance, multimedia operations, and budget oversight.”
- Combine the strongest achievements into 4–5 bullets, prioritizing measurable impact: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal site serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more outcome-based: add email/social growth, engagement, campaign performance, or production volume if available; otherwise trim “tens of thousands/thousands” language.
- Strengthen verbs and business value: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio, increasing internal production capacity for advocacy, events, and recurring video content”; “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery reporting to improve executive decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry.
- Video-program expansion also appears in earlier NACo roles; emphasize the studio build and scaled capacity here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry reads generic and overlaps with both the more senior Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager/Producer role. Tighten it around operational leadership, newsletter ownership, and the launch/expansion of repeatable advocacy video.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and function: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social, and video, improving editorial coordination and advocacy messaging across NACo.”
- Make bullets more outcome-oriented: “Owned four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Sharpen the video bullet: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger systems statement: “Improved cross-team editorial planning and digital publishing workflows across communications, advocacy, and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Helping scale” and “helped improve” sound soft; use direct ownership language.
- Avoid repeating broader channel oversight and governance language already covered more strongly in the Director of Digital Media role.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. It should be tightened to emphasize senior-level strategic scope rather than repeat broad communications language.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic phrases with sharper, differentiated wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy & web modernization
- Editorial governance, publishing systems & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy campaigns & stakeholder messaging
- Audience strategy, content planning & information architecture
- Consider reducing to 4 lines by merging related ideas; “audience-focused content planning” is too soft/generic for this level.
- Use parallel noun phrases throughout; avoid mixing leadership terms with tactical descriptors.
- If space allows, align wording to recent impact areas: governance, modernization, AI/search, analytics-enabled operations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” substantially duplicate Core Competencies.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” repeats language already established in the header and work experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and recent execution themes rather than repeat every technology.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters: “Drupal & enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations & workflow automation • SharePoint / Power Pages • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Drop “WordPress” and “jQuery” here unless they are central to target roles; they feel less differentiating than Drupal, CMS modernization, and AI/search.
- Use “front-end implementation” instead of listing all languages if you want a more senior tone.
- If space allows, prioritize recent strengths tied to experience: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, analytics-connected integrations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills strategic and let the Technical section hold the full tool inventory.
- “Workflow automation” and “AI-enabled search experiences” already appear in Core Competencies; avoid repeating exact phrasing if possible.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for the recent NACo leadership roles, but it reads as a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with “Technical + IT.” Make it more outcome-oriented and slightly more strategic.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio and Microsoft Clarity for analytics infrastructure, dashboarding and user-behavior insights”
- Replace generic items with stronger phrasing: “KPI framework development” instead of “KPI design”; “executive reporting” instead of “Leadership reporting”
- Tighten final item to “SEO and digital performance optimization” for clearer scope
- Optional full version: “Analytics infrastructure (GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity) • KPI framework development • Executive reporting • SEO and digital performance optimization”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; keep Topline Skills more strategic and let Technical + IT hold the full tool inventory.
- “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating the same wording exactly.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize operational leadership and recent in-house studio/event delivery impact rather than listing basic production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from task list to higher-value capability language: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio operations • PTZ camera and multi-camera workflows”
- Replace “Video production and editing” with a more senior phrasing such as “Broadcast-quality video production” or “End-to-end video production” to better match Director-level experience.
- Consider adding one outcome-oriented qualifier if space allows: “supporting advocacy programming and recurring multimedia content.”
- Keep only 4 concise bullets max; remove filler and avoid tool-level detail already covered elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” / “multimedia production” already appears in Core Competencies; use this section to be more specific, not repetitive.
- PTZ/studio details also overlap with “Livestream studio workflows” in Technical + IT, so avoid expanding into tool lists here.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platforms, but this item is too generic and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” skills section. It should either add level/context or be tightened to emphasize current, high-value platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages** → keep Drupal first and consider dropping GitHub Pages unless used professionally.
- Add proficiency/context if space allows: **Drupal (enterprise migration, modular microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages**
- If you want stronger impact, rename to **CMS & Web Platforms** and align with recent work: **Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages**
- Consider separating lightweight/static tools from CMSs: move **GitHub Pages** to Coding & Technical Implementation or remove it.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely repeats **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; keep one version broader and this one more concise.
- Drupal already appears prominently in recent NACo roles, so avoid overemphasizing it in multiple places without new detail.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical breadth, but this item reads like a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” For a senior digital leader, emphasize implementation tools you actively use in recent work and group them more strategically.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery • Integration & deployment: API integrations, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions • Tagging & tracking: Google Tag Manager”
- Consider dropping version-specific “HTML5/CSS3” unless the rest of the CV uses versioning; “HTML, CSS” is cleaner.
- If accurate, add scope/context instead of more tools, e.g., “for Drupal microsites, analytics tagging, and workflow automation.”
- If space allows elsewhere, tie one tool to impact in experience bullets rather than here, e.g., GTM for analytics rollout or Workers for performance/automation.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Workflow automation” and GitHub Actions may also overlap with the Automation & Workflow Systems section.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than reinforcing your stronger positioning in workflow automation and cross-team operations. Tighten it around systems you actively use to build processes, not just collaborate.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Systems**
- Reorder by strategic relevance: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello • Slack • Microsoft Teams**  
- Drop **Basecamp** unless it was used recently or materially; it feels older/lower-signal than the others.
- If space allows, add light qualifiers to show application, e.g. **Airtable (workflow systems), Power Automate/Zapier (process automation), Jira/Asana/Trello (project operations)**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with **Core Competencies: Workflow automation and platform integration** and **Topline Skills: Workflow automation / Airtable systems**; keep this section tool-focused and avoid repeating capability language elsewhere.
- **Slack** and **Teams** are lower-value if space is tight; they’re common collaboration tools, not differentiators.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Relevant tools, but the item is too generic and misses the strongest signal from recent roles: enterprise email/engagement platform leadership in a high-volume communications environment. It should emphasize scale and primary systems, not read like a basic software list.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by likely depth/relevance from recent work: **Higher Logic • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope qualifiers: **Higher Logic (newsletter and member communications) • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (campaign automation) • Mailchimp**
- Consider renaming the heading to sharpen value: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms** or **Email, CRM & Engagement Systems**
- If space allows elsewhere, tie to outcomes rather than here: e.g., “managed weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands” belongs in experience, not this skills line.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item overlaps with work-experience bullets about newsletters and digital channels; keep this line tool-focused only.
- “Engagement” may partially overlap with “Automation & Workflow Systems,” so avoid adding automation language here unless platform-specific.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills” and the Director role. Tighten it to emphasize analysis/optimization capabilities rather than repeating platform names alone.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Analytics, Reporting & Optimization**
- Rewrite as: **GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • KPI design • dashboard development • SEO/performance analysis • A/B testing**
- Replace vague **“Dashboarding”** with **“dashboard development”** or **“executive reporting”** for stronger phrasing.
- If space allows, group by function for readability: **Analytics platforms:** GA4, Clarity, BigQuery | **Reporting:** Looker Studio, Power BI | **Optimization:** SEO, A/B testing, KPI design

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is nearly identical to **Topline Skills → Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider keeping detail in one place and shortening the other.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid repeating the exact same list elsewhere.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and useful scope, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and anchor it in “firsts,” team-building, and concrete outputs.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize early-career buildout: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Tighten the second sentence around visible contributions: “Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates, to expand the organization’s in-house publishing capacity.”
- Replace “high-impact” with specifics if available: add counts/frequency (e.g., number of livestreams, weekly series duration, audience growth, email/social output).
- Clarify supervision scope: “Provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate” or quantify if you managed workload/training.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; frame this item as launching or early producing, and the later role as scaling.
- “Strengthening workflows” repeats language used in later NACo entries; here, stress foundational setup rather than mature operations.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows the start of your multimedia/digital trajectory, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo roles. Emphasize the “first podcast” achievement and tighten the research/program support language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout outcome: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination, and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with a clearer scope: “Produced digital and multimedia content to support program communications and policy storytelling.”
- If possible, add one measurable detail: number of episodes, audience, stakeholders supported, or types of projects delivered.
- Keep this entry shorter than later NACo roles so the progression into digital leadership remains clear.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later video/multimedia bullets; keep this item focused on podcast launch and innovation/project coordination.
- Avoid repeating broad “supported organizational programs and policy work” language used elsewhere unless you can specify outputs or impact.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills list, but it reads more like a mixed capability bucket than a clean tools section. It also overlaps with stronger, more recent multimedia leadership already shown in work experience and Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
